## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

# Phaser 4 WebGL: migrate core `GeometryMask` sites to Mask filters + scaffold `Phaser.AUTO`

Raised from `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (Main Street repo, `../tce-main-street`) on producer
instruction (2026-10-29, "separate core item in `../Tableau-Card-Engine`").

## Problem statement

Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7` made `GameObject.setMask` a **no-op under WebGL**.
`node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/components/Mask.js:27` states
`GeometryMask` is Canvas-only; the WebGL path logs

```
Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.
```

and returns immediately, so the object renders **unclipped**.

The Main Street game repo has completed its side of the migration
(`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`, commit `73cfba6c` on its `dev`) and has switched its
launcher from `Phaser.CANVAS` to `Phaser.AUTO`. That change makes this defect
live in shipped builds: the core-owned overlays below lose their scroll
clipping in any WebGL boot.

Outstanding core-owned call sites (verified 2026-10-29 against core `f0b5b9e9`):

- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — `setMask` at the scroll-region setup
  (observed at `SettingsPanel.ts:574` during a real WebGL boot)
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — `setupScrollMask` (observed at `HelpPanel.ts:386`)
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts` — `setMask` / `createGeometryMask` in the overlay dialog
  scroll region
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` — `setMask`
  (reached via `GymSceneBase.initHelp`)

Additionally the scaffold generator still forces Canvas, so every downstream
game repo it generates reverts the migration:

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderMainTs()` emits `type: Phaser.CANVAS`
- the core repo's own `main.ts` likewise

## Users

- **Game players** — Help / Settings / Overlay dialogs and the Gym card index
  must stay visually correct (content clipped to its scroll region) in WebGL
  builds, not just in Canvas ones.
- **Downstream game-repo maintainers** — need the scaffold to emit
  `Phaser.AUTO` so a fresh/re-scaffolded repo does not silently regress to
  Canvas and lose access to Phaser 4's Filter/GPU-shader pipeline.
- **Maintainers** — one shared core helper instead of per-repo copies.

## Reference implementation (already proven, do not re-invent)

`../tce-main-street/src/ContainerClip.ts` is the working pattern and is the
model to port into core as a shared, exported helper:

- `createContainerClip(scene, target, rect?)` branches once on
  `scene.renderer.type`:
  - **Canvas**: unchanged `GeometryMask` (transparent fill, Graphics on the
    display list) — Canvas output stays byte-stable.
  - **WebGL**: `target.enableFilters()` then
    `target.filters.internal.addMask(graphics, false, scene.cameras.main)`,
    with an **opaque** fill and the Graphics kept **off the display list**
    (a Mask filter samples the mask texture's alpha and renders the mask
    GameObject itself).
- **`clear()` is a real "no clip"** (Canvas `clearMask`, WebGL
  `filter.active = false`). A zero-area mask is *not* a no-op — it hides the
  whole object.
- A `Container` has no intrinsic width/height, so Phaser focuses the filter on
  the camera context and the mask applies in **screen space**, matching Canvas
  `GeometryMask` semantics (fixed to the scene, not following the object).
- Tear down the clip on scene shutdown: under WebGL the mask Graphics is off
  the display list and is not disposed by the scene.
- Verified by evidence: a Mask filter **does** clip a `Container` in rc.7;
  proven with `renderer.snapshotPixel()` probes inside/outside the rect, and
  unchanged when the clipped container is translated. No per-camera-viewport
  fallback is needed.

Do not edit the Main Street repo from this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Core helper.** A renderer-aware container-clip helper exists in core
   (suggested `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts`), exported through the public `@ui`
   surface so downstream game repos can reuse it, with the `ContainerClip`
   API (`setRect`, `clear`, `destroy`) and the Canvas/WebGL branching described
   above. Its doc comment records the Phaser 4 Canvas-only `setMask`
   restriction.
2. **Sites migrated.** `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `src/ui/Overlay.ts`,
   `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` and `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts`
   no longer construct a `GeometryMask` directly for clipping; all four use the
   shared helper.
3. **Scaffold emits `Phaser.AUTO`.** `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`
   `renderMainTs()` emits `type: Phaser.AUTO`, the core repo's own `main.ts`
   matches, and any scaffold test/fixture asserting `Phaser.CANVAS` is updated.
4. **WebGL browser test.** At least one browser test forces `Phaser.WEBGL` and
   asserts (a) clipping actually happens (pixel probe via
   `renderer.snapshotPixel()`) and (b) **no** `setMask … not supported in
   WebGL` warning is emitted from core code. Canvas parity is asserted in the
   same file.
5. **No Canvas regression.** Full core test suite green; Canvas rendering
   output unchanged (the Canvas branch keeps `GeometryMask`).
6. **Docs.** The renderer/mask restriction is documented (core README and/or
   `docs/`) so the next reader does not repeat the diagnosis, and the scaffold
   documentation states the emitted renderer.
7. **Downstream switch-over hand-off.** On completion, a work item is created
   (or the existing placeholder updated) in the Main Street repo
   (`../tce-main-street`) to: bump the pinned core commit in
   `configs/engine-pin.json`, run `npm run scaffold` to regenerate
   `main.ts`, re-run `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts`
   with the core-owned warnings no longer excluded, and confirm the launcher
   boots WebGL with no unclipped core overlay.
   **The follow-up already exists**: `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7` ("Re-scaffold Main
   Street launcher to Phaser.AUTO and verify a clean WebGL boot once core masks
   land") in the Main Street store, currently `blocked`. Reuse/update that item
   rather than creating a second one, and leave a comment on it naming the core
   commit that satisfies this item.

## Constraints

- Do **not** edit the Main Street repo (`../tce-main-street`) from this item;
  the cross-repo hand-off is a work-item, not a code edit (AC7).
- Canvas behaviour must not change: branch on the renderer, do not replace the
  `GeometryMask` path.
- No new dependencies.
- `TestGamePool` and downstream browser tests intentionally stay on
  `Phaser.CANVAS` for CI speed (~10x faster under SwiftShader) — do not force
  them to WebGL.

## Existing state / verified facts

- Phaser pin: `4.0.0-rc.7`. `GameObject` mixes in `Components.Filters`
  (`enableFilters()`, `filters`), so any GameObject — `Container` included —
  can host a Mask filter.
- `GeometryMask` uses the Graphics **path** and ignores fill alpha; a Mask
  filter uses the rendered mask texture's **alpha**.
- `filterList.getActive()` filters on `filter.active`, so `active = false` is a
  cheap way to disable a clip without destroying it.

## Key Files

- `docs/ui/renderer-aware-clipping.md` — "Downstream switch-over (Main
  Street hand-off)": records `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7`, the delivering core
  commits and the completed switch-over (AC7, commit `9fd4774d`).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — cross-links that record from the renderer
  guidance.
- `src/ui/createCardGame.ts` — the `Phaser.AUTO` render-type default the
  launcher now boots through (`type: renderType ?? Phaser.AUTO`).
- `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts` — the shared helper the consumer imports as
  `@ui/ContainerClip`.

## Related work

- `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (Main Street) — renderer migration + renderer-aware
  clips for the in-repo surfaces; delivered commit `73cfba6c`. Source of this
  item.
- `MS-0MVT4M9KM005Z0YM` (Main Street) — the original diagnosis; closed as a
  duplicate of `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`, with its core-owned part routed here.
- `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` (Main Street) — the earlier core-deferral record for
  `HelpPanel` / `Overlay` / `SettingsPanel`; superseded by this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: filter cost.** Each clipped container gains a filter render step
  (context-sized for unbounded containers). Mitigation: measure in the browser
  test scene; keep the clip count small (4 sites).
- **Risk: Mask filter on a nested/transformed container.** The Main Street
  evidence covers transformed containers; re-verify per core site with a pixel
  probe rather than assuming.
- **Assumption:** headless Chromium (Playwright) provides WebGL2 in CI, so the
  WebGL browser test is viable.
data.title: Phaser 4 WebGL: migrate core GeometryMask sites to Mask filters + scaffold Phaser.AUTO

# Scaffold generator: opt-in write gating and an explicit game-path migration flag

## Goal

As the engine maintainer, I want `game-repo-scaffold.ts` to stop overwriting
consumer-owned wiring by default and to stop applying the
`example-games/<game>/` → `src/` codemod to every file on every run, so a
re-scaffold of the live `tce-main-street` checkout can no longer silently gut
its build/test wiring.

Created from `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` (producer decision Q2=A). That item's
acceptance criteria are carried over here in full; the `MS` item is closed once
this item exists.

## Producer decisions (2026-10-31)

- **Q1 = B — explicit selection, not a changed default.** Keep today's
  behaviour for fresh/extracted game repos; add `--only <file,...>`, `--force`
  and `--dry-run`; the main-street `scaffold` script opts in to `main.ts` only.
- **Q2 = A — this item owns the generator change**, test-first in the engine
  repo, followed by an engine pin bump in `tce-main-street`.
- **Q3 = A — `rewriteGameTreePaths` becomes opt-in** via
  `--migrate-game-paths` (default off); fresh repos are already renamed by
  `extract-repos.sh --path-rename`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Generator write gating.** `scaffoldGameRepo`/the CLI accept
   `--only <file,...>` (restrict the run to the named generated files; no other
   file, symlink or rewrite is performed), `--force` (allow overwriting a file
   whose content differs from the template) and `--dry-run` (report every file
   as `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`, writing nothing). Default
   behaviour for extracted repos is unchanged: a full scaffold still writes all
   generated files.
2. **Write reporting.** Every run (dry or real) prints a machine-readable
   summary of the classification per file, so a consumer can see what a run
   would touch before trusting it.
3. **Path rewrite is opt-in.** `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` and the
   accompanying quoted-path/alias rewrites run only with
   `--migrate-game-paths`; without it, no file under `tests/` or `src/` is
   modified. `--migrate-game-paths` also reports the files it rewrites.
4. **Engine tests (test-first).** `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
   gains tests written **before** the implementation for: `--only` restricting
   writes, `--dry-run` writing nothing while classifying correct, `--force`
   required to replace a diverged file, default-on-path-rewrite removed
   (no-op without the flag) and preserved with the flag. The full engine suite
   passes.
5. **Main-street consumer wiring.** In the `tce-main-street` checkout:
   `package.json`'s `scaffold` script passes `--only main.ts` (plus the flag
   name chosen in AC1); `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` copies
   this repo's `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`,
   `env.d.ts`, `main.ts` and representative `tests/` files into a temporary
   directory, runs the scaffold against it and fails if any protected wiring
   file changes (while asserting `main.ts` is regenerated);
   `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` replaces the interim "classify-and-revert"
   rule with the new default and opt-in. All related documentation is updated
   (code comments in the generator explain why the overwrite is gated; any
   README or docs-site text describing the scaffold command is corrected).
6. **Stability and validation.** `npm run scaffold` in `tce-main-street` twice in
   a row leaves `git status --porcelain` empty except for opted-in paths; the
   engine pin bump (gitlink + `configs/engine-pin.json` together) is a
   deliberate commit in `tce-main-street`; `npm run build` and the changed-scope
   gate pass there; the full project test suite passes.

## Scope and delivery (two repos)

1. **Engine repo (`Tableau-Card-Engine`, `dev`)** — generator change +
   engine-side tests (AC1–AC4). This is the item's primary worktree.
2. **Consumer repo (`tce-main-street`, `dev`)** — script wiring, regression
   test, docs, engine pin bump (AC5–AC6).

If worktree isolation prevents editing `tce-main-street` from this item's
worktree, create an `MS` follow-up item during planning that carries AC5–AC6
verbatim and link it here; AC5–AC6 must never be dropped.

## Constraints

- **Do not change the default for extracted repos.** The eight sibling repos
  (`tce-golf` etc.) keep the plain `scaffold` invocation and must still receive
  template updates from a full run.
- **Never run the destructive path** against a live checkout while developing;
  experiment in a temp directory or the worktree.
- **Engine pin discipline:** the pin (`configs/engine-pin.json`) and the `core`
  gitlink travel together in one deliberate commit; never a build side effect.
- Repository boundaries: only the generator, its tests, the consumer
  `package.json`/docs/tests and the engine pin are in scope.

## Existing state

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`: `writeFile()` writes unconditionally
  (no content comparison, no dry-run, no allow-list); `parseArgs` supports only
  `--game`, `--game-repo-root`, `--core-root`, `--core-rel`, `--version`,
  `--all`, `--repos-dir`, `--layout`.
- `rewriteGameTreePaths()` walks all of `tests/**` and `src/**` and applies four
  textual rewrites to every `.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs/.js` file whether or not it
  references the game tree.
- `index.html` is copied verbatim from `core/index.html`; `renderPackageJson`
  inherits the core's scripts and dependencies — both clobber local wiring in a
  live checkout.
- One observed run on a clean `dev` tree rewrote 11 files besides `main.ts`,
  including the drift guard's own `STALE_PREFIX`, a run-tests import (`→
  @core-scripts/run-tests`) and 250 lines of documented LOCAL SURGICAL
  ADDITIONS in `vite.config.ts`. Full table on `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB`.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 "Write gating" →
  "Consumer verification (tce-main-street, recorded 2026-11-03)": the
  recorded AC6 verification (double `npm run scaffold` clean tree, the
  pin+gitlink commit, the consumer build and suite), delivered by
  `CG-0MW1AHY0A00697AI` in commit `0f7b5e1d`.
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — write gating (`--only`, `--force`,
  `--dry-run`), classification reporting, `--migrate-game-paths` gating in
  `scaffoldGameRepo` + `parseArgs`, rationale comments.
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — engine-side tests (AC4).
- `tce-main-street/package.json` — scope the `scaffold` script.
- `tce-main-street/tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` — new
  regression guard (temp-copy harness); follow the style of
  `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts`.
- `tce-main-street/docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — document default + opt-in.
- `tce-main-street/configs/engine-pin.json` — pin bump.
- `tce-main-street/main.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html` —
  protected inputs for the regression harness (not to be edited).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `main.ts` is the only file main-street currently wants
  regenerated (per `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH`).
- **Risk:** a cross-repo delivery from one worktree may violate worktree
  isolation — mitigated by the explicit split-and-link rule above.
- **Risk:** `--only` interacting with symlink/asset linking could leave a repo
  half-scaffolded — mitigate by making `--only` skip links entirely and
  reporting that it did.
- **Risk:** temp-copy harness drift — mitigate by copying real repo files rather
  than inlining fixtures.
- **Scope-creep risk:** generator script hygiene (broken `scaffold:game` keys)
  is tracked separately in `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0`; link, do not absorb.

## Related work

- `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` — origin item (intake brief, producer decisions,
  observed damage table). Closed on creation of this item.
- `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH` / `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7` — the re-scaffold that exposed
  the hazard.
- `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0` and children — generator-emitted script hygiene
  (separate scope).
- `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` — template improvement that relies on re-scaffold
  remaining usable.
- `CG-0MVPWPWLA008FTDJ`, `CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA` — precedent template fixes that
  re-scaffold propagates.

## Plan (2026-10-31)

**Decomposition — five child items, test-first inside each slice.** Test-first is satisfied *within* each child (failing tests authored first, then the implementation, then a green build → test → commit cycle); no standalone RED child exists because this repo gates every commit on a green suite, so a tests-only child could not be committed. The children cut vertically through the layers they touch: generator code, generator tests, CLI `--help`, and the rationale/doc prose that belongs to the slice. Consumer prose lives in the engine docs child; the consumer repo work is the MS follow-up.

| # | Child | Slice | Parent ACs |
|---|-------|-------|------------|
| 1 | `CG-0MVWGJNQM0061W6I` Scaffold write classification, dry-run and report | classification pipeline, `--dry-run`, `--json` report, typed `ScaffoldResult.files` | AC1 (`--dry-run`), AC2, AC4 |
| 2 | `CG-0MVWGJPPA000GBE7` Only allow-list, force and skip-local gating | `--only`, `--force`, `skip-local`, side-effect suppression, fail-fast name validation | AC1, AC4 |
| 3 | `CG-0MVWGJRIO0094Y4Z` Gate path rewrite behind migrate-game-paths | `--migrate-game-paths` opt-in, dry-run preview, mutual exclusion with `--only` | AC3, AC4 |
| 4 | `CG-0MVWGJTDL00576GQ` Document scaffold write gating in engine docs | `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, generator header cross-reference | AC5 (docs clause) |
| 5 | `CG-0MVWGJUU3003J7HA` Main-street wiring, guard, docs and pin bump | cross-repo delivery, tracked as `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` (AC5 + AC6 verbatim) | AC5, AC6 |

**Dependency order:** 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 (`wl dep add` edges wired). Child 5 is a tracking/verification child: the code, test, doc and pin-bump work is executed in `tce-main-street` under `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`, because this item's worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-…`) cannot write outside the core checkout — the parent's own scope note requires exactly this split, and AC5–AC6 must not be dropped.

**Recorded design decision (AC1's `--force` interaction).** AC1 lists `--force` and the `skip-local` classification, while the Constraints require a plain full run to keep propagating template updates to the eight sibling repos. The only reading in which both hold — and in which `--force` is not dead code — is:

- **No `--only`** → today's behaviour: every diverged generated file is rewritten (`update`). Implemented as `effectiveForce = force || only === undefined`.
- **With `--only`** → only the named files are candidates; a named file that exists and differs is `skip-local` (untouched) unless `--force` is passed, and every unselected file is `skip-local`. Selection mode suppresses the `core` symlink, shared-asset links, root app-icon links and the game-tree path rewrite entirely.
- `--only` + `--migrate-game-paths` is rejected as a conflict (selection promises "no rewrite").

Consequence: the `tce-main-street` scaffold script becomes `--only main.ts --force` (AC5's "plus the flag name chosen in AC1"). This interpretation is implemented by children 2–3 and consumed by `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`; it is recorded here so the audit can check intent rather than re-derive it.

**Other recorded assumptions**

- `main.ts` is the only file `tce-main-street` wants regenerated (per `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH`); `configs/game.json` may be opted in later by the same mechanism.
- `--json` is the machine-readable report surface (one document per run: an object for `--game`, an array for `--all`); the classification vocabulary stays exactly `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`.
- The generator's script-hygiene defects (`scaffold:game` keys) stay with `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0` — linked, not absorbed.

**Duplicate check:** `wl search scaffold` / `wl search "scaffold generator write gating"` against the core store returned no non-terminal overlapping item; the closest completed items (`CG-0MVSIB5LH0069LB3`, `CG-0MVPWPWLA008FTDJ`, `CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA`) are template fixes this plan's full-run back-compatibility must keep propagating.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The producer answered the design questions on `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` (2026-10-31) before this item was created; that record is the authoritative source and is not re-asked here.

- Q1: "Should the generator change its default, or expose explicit selection while keeping today's default?" Answer (producer): "**B — explicit selection, not a changed default.** Keep today's behaviour for fresh/extracted game repos; add `--only <file,...>`, `--force` and `--dry-run`; the main-street `scaffold` script opts in to `main.ts` only." Final: B.
- Q2: "Which repo owns the generator change, and does it also own the consumer wiring?" Answer (producer): "**A — this item owns the generator change**, test-first in the engine repo, followed by an engine pin bump in `tce-main-street`." Final: A.
- Q3: "Should `rewriteGameTreePaths` stay on by default?" Answer (producer): "**A — `rewriteGameTreePaths` becomes opt-in** via `--migrate-game-paths` (default off); fresh repos are already renamed by `extract-repos.sh --path-rename`." Final: A.
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Does a selected file that diverges from the template get written unconditionally, or only with `--force`?" Answer (plan, from AC1 + the extracted-repo constraint): only with `--force`; a full run keeps today's unconditional rewrite. Recorded as the "Recorded design decision" above. Evidence: AC1 (`--force` "allow overwriting a file whose content differs from the template"), Constraints ("the eight sibling repos … must still receive template updates from a full run").
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Can `tce-main-street` be edited from this item's worktree?" Answer (plan, from the parent's scope note + worktree isolation): no — create the `MS` follow-up `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` carrying AC5–AC6 verbatim. Final: MS follow-up created.
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Which consumer docs still describe the scaffold command?" Answer (plan, repo inspection): `tce-main-street/docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (re-scaffold references) and `tce-main-street/docs/dev/testing.md` (three passages claiming `npm run scaffold` regenerates the `resolve.dedupe` and transcript-persist wiring). The MS follow-up corrects both; the engine docs child covers `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `README.md`.

**OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for the audit review):** none — the flagged interpretation above is an implementation detail inside the producer's fixed design space, documented rather than escalated.
data.title: Scaffold generator: opt-in write gating and an explicit game-path migration flag

# `engine-sync.sync --soft`: an interactive dev-start mode that never blocks on a dirty `./core`

## Problem statement

`scripts/engine-sync.mjs` exposes one sync mode whose first act is a hard guard:

```js
if (submoduleIsDirty(repoRoot, coreRel)) {
  throw new EngineSyncError(`engine:sync: ${coreRel} has uncommitted changes — refusing to sync (never clobber). …`);
}
```

That is correct for build paths (`npm run build`, `build:electron`, `implement.py finish`, the dev-push gate) where a dirty submodule must fail loudly. It makes the same function unusable for an **interactive dev start**: a game repo wants `npm run dev` to compose the current engine `dev` tip, but `./core` is routinely dirty while someone works engine-side, so a strict sync would refuse to start the server exactly when the developer needs it.

Operator decision (this session, Q1) is **option B**: add a soft mode rather than wiring the strict `engine:sync` into `dev`.

## Users / user stories

- **Game developer (downstream `tce-<game>` repo):** "As a game developer, `npm run dev` composes the current engine `dev` tip and starts serving, without me running a build or doing submodule surgery first."
- **Engine developer (dirty `./core`):** "As a developer with uncommitted engine edits, `npm run dev` still starts on my working tree, with a loud warning that the engine sync was skipped — my changes are never clobbered or blocked."
- **Release operator (unchanged):** "As a release operator, nothing about `engine:verify` or the strict `engine:sync` build path changes; a dirty submodule still fails a release/build loudly."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `syncEngine({ …, soft: true })` and the CLI `node scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft` exist. With a **dirty** `./core` they perform **no git operation**, log a loud, actionable warning naming the submodule and the reason, and return/exit `0` with `{ updated: false, … , skipped: 'dirty' }` (or equivalent documented field) instead of throwing.
2. Strict mode is **byte-for-byte unchanged**: `sync` without `--soft` (and `syncEngine()` with no `soft` key) still throws the existing `EngineSyncError` message on a dirty submodule, so `npm run build` / `build:electron` / the finish gate keep their current failure semantics (regression-tested).
3. Soft mode changes **only** the dirty-guard outcome. Every other path is identical to strict sync: clean + remote ahead → `git submodule update --remote`, loud `from → to` log, pin rewrite when the repo is pinned, return `updated`; offline/unreachable remote → warn and keep the checkout (already soft); clean + already at tip → no pin write. A dirty-submodule soft run must **not** rewrite the pin or stage the gitlink.
4. `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (`renderPackageJson`) emits the two scripts that let a game repo use soft mode:
   - `dev: "npm run engine:dev-sync && vite --host"`
   - `engine:dev-sync: "node <coreRel>/scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft"`
   and the rendered `package.json` for `main-street` matches the committed `tce-main-street/package.json` for those two entries.
5. `scripts/engine-sync.d.mts` types are updated (`soft?: boolean` on the sync options, the new result field, `SyncResult` doc comment) and `tsc --noEmit` passes for consumers of the declarations.
6. Engine-side tests in `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` cover: (a) dirty submodule + `soft: true` → resolves, no throw, no update, no pin write, warning reported; (b) dirty submodule + strict → still throws the existing message; (c) clean submodule + `soft: true` → same result as strict (update + pin rewrite + staging); (d) CLI `sync --soft` exit code `0` with the warning on stdout/stderr and `sync` exit code `1` on the same fixture; (e) scaffold render assertion for the two scripts (extend the existing render test).
7. CLI usage text documents `--soft` and its dev-start intent; `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (engine) describes the two modes (strict = build/release gate, soft = interactive dev start) wherever `engine:sync` is documented, and the canonical script header comment is updated.
8. All related documentation is updated (engine `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, script docblocks, npm-script comments in the scaffold template).
9. Full project test suite passes; `npm run build` (strict TypeScript + Vite) succeeds.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo ordering:** the engine commit lands on engine `dev` **first**; the downstream gitlink bump + `configs/engine-pin.json` re-pin is tracked in the paired `tce-main-street` item — do not bump from here.
- **No new failure semantics for gates.** Soft mode must be opt-in per call site; no build/release script may use it.
- **Never clobber.** Soft mode's dirty outcome is "skip and warn", never "stash/reset/checkout over" the developer's edits.
- **Scaffold ownership:** the `dev` / `engine:dev-sync` scripts belong in `renderPackageJson`, never hand-edited into a game repo's `package.json`.
- **Do not disturb the dirty engine checkout** at `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` — its main checkout currently has 3 modified `example-games/gym/content/*` files from unrelated work; work in the implement worktree.
- Tests are run through the test skill (`run_tests.py`), never ad hoc.
- UK English in all written output.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — "Consumer wiring (rendered == committed)" in the
  engine-sync section records the rendered `dev` / `engine:dev-sync`
  values, their byte-identical match with `tce-main-street/package.json`
  (AC6) and the `npm run build` verification (AC11); delivered by
  `CG-0MW1AHY0A00697AI` in commit `0f7b5e1d`.
- `scripts/engine-sync.mjs` — `syncEngine({ soft })`, CLI `--soft` flag parsing + usage text, header docblock describing strict vs soft.
- `scripts/engine-sync.d.mts` — `soft?: boolean`, result field, doc comments.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `dev` + `engine:dev-sync` in `renderPackageJson` with an explanatory comment.
- `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` — soft/strict/dirty/clean/CLI cases (fixtures already exist for sync/verify).
- scaffold render test (`grep renderPackageJson` in `tests/scripts/`) — assert the two rendered scripts.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine-sync mode table (strict vs soft) and the "when to use which" rule.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: soft mode masks a stale engine.** Mitigation: the warning is loud and names the reason; strict build paths still catch lag at `engine:verify`/pin. No silent success.
- **Risk: two modes drift.** Mitigation: one code path with a single conditional on the dirty-guard outcome, proven by tests (a) and (c) asserting result equality with strict mode.
- **Risk: game repos start staging pin/gitlink bumps on every `npm run dev`.** Accepted (the pin travels with the gitlink by policy, CG-0MVO268500071BPI) and mitigated by the existing loud `from → to` / pin-log lines; recorded in the paired downstream item.
- **Risk: npm script name proliferation.** Bounded to one wrapper (`engine:dev-sync`) that exists only so `dev` can pass `--soft`; `engine:sync` keeps its meaning.
- **Assumption:** downstream repos invoke the script exactly as scaffolded (`node ./core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft`), so no arguments ever reach `dev` from npm.

## Related work

- **CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q** — original engine-sync/verify + scaffold wiring (strict sync in `build`, `verify` in `build:release`); this item adds the opt-in soft mode it did not need then.
- **CG-0MVO268500071BPI** — pin-tracks-tip policy: the pin and the `./core` gitlink always travel together.
- **CG-0MVTVSYQE002JGDN** — git hermeticity contract (`REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`) that soft mode must keep honouring.
- **CG-0MVOCF9T5007CH2A** — local-suite coverage of the pin policy and lag-vs-bad-pin diagnostics (pattern for the new tests).
- **CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN** — current in-flight engine item; unrelated, listed to avoid worktree collisions.

## Appendix: decision record

- **Q1 — how should an interactive dev start compose the engine?** Options: (A) strict `npm run engine:sync && vite --host` (dev fails loudly on a dirty submodule); (B) opt-in soft sync mode used by `dev`, strict paths untouched; (C) hand-edit only the game repo's `package.json` (clobbered by re-scaffold). **Answer (operator, this session): B.** Source: producer chat — "Make run dev also run engine:sync" → presented options A/B/C with consequences → "B".
data.title: engine-sync: add a --soft sync mode for interactive dev starts (never block on a dirty ./core)

# Game-repo scaffold must wire git hooks and emit a full-suite pre-push variant

discovered-from: MS-0MVTI7F5R009OQ14 (tce-main-street)

> **Scope (producer decision, 2026-11-03):** narrowed to the **Tableau-Card-Engine** repo only. The framework hook content and `install_pi.sh` selection are owned by **`SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`** (SorraAgents); this item wires the *scaffold* to activate hooks, seeds thresholds, and verifies the unified gate in a real game repo. **Blocked-by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`.**

## Problem statement

Game repos generated by the engine scaffold (`scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) receive a committed `.githooks/` directory but **no activation**: the scaffold never sets `core.hooksPath`, so git ignores the committed hooks in every fresh clone until someone runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` by hand. The scaffold also generates no `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`, so the context-budget gate is fail-open, and it ships the gate-less **v2** hook rather than the full-suite gate. The full-suite hook *content* (local-then-global runner resolution) is delivered by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`; this item makes the scaffold **produce a push-gated repo that consumes that unified hook** with no manual per-clone activation.

## Users / user stories

- As a **game producer/agent**, I want a freshly scaffolded game repo to have active git hooks, so branch policy, worklog sync and the context-budget gate work without a manual per-clone step.
- As the **producer**, I want scaffolded repos to ship the full-suite pre-push gate, so "pushed to `dev`" means "green at this git state" and the audit skill can reuse a real cache entry.
- As a **framework maintainer**, I want the scaffold and `install_pi.sh` to agree on one hook variant, so game-repo hooks do not drift from the framework's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Scaffold wires hooks and thresholds.** `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks` in generated repos, installs the full-suite pre-push hook (the unified v3 content from `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`), and generates/commits `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` from the new repo's measured surface. *Metric: scaffold a throwaway repo in a temp dir; assert `git config --get core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves inside `.githooks`, the generated `.githooks/pre-push` carries the full-suite gate (not the gate-less v2), and the thresholds file exists and passes `measure_context.py`.*
- **AC2 — Worktree-safe under `--strict-git-env`.** A push from a linked worktree of a scaffolded repo runs the gate and is gated, with no `--strict-git-env` refusal. *Metric: end-to-end test pushes from a linked worktree with a stub runner and asserts the suite is invoked and the push is gated (git-exported worktree-managed `GIT_DIR` exempt; see `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9).*
- **AC3 — Rollout verified in a real game repo and documented.** Re-run the scaffold/installer against `../tce-main-street`, confirm `core.hooksPath` and the full-suite gate on a real `dev` push (a gate-produced full-suite cache entry exists), and update the scaffold/README notes plus TCE-owned docs. *Metric: rollout evidence recorded on this item; docs updated; full engine suite passes.*
- **AC4 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and the TCE-owned `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (scaffold activation, threshold generation, the one-activation-step-on-fresh-clone caveat). Stale claims that game repos cannot have the gate are removed.
- **AC5 — Tests green.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (run via the test skill).

## Constraints

- **Tableau-Card-Engine repo only.** The framework hook content and `install_pi.sh` selection live in SorraAgents under `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`; do **not** edit SorraAgents from this item. Consume that item's unified v3 hook.
- POSIX `sh` hook; no new runtime dependencies; the hook must keep working on a bare git checkout.
- Do not weaken the existing v2 gates (branch policy, context budget, worklog sync) or their bypass variables.
- Keep the gate fail-*closed* for a missing runner on `dev`/`main`; fail-open remains acceptable only for optional tooling (context-budget measurement).
- Preserve scaffold idempotence. Setting `core.hooksPath` is **local config**, so the scaffold must document that a fresh clone still needs one activation step (`install_pi.sh` or `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`).
- Respect the project test-execution policy: no ad-hoc suite invocation; use the test skill.

## Existing state

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — no `githooks` / `hooksPath` / thresholds handling (grep returns nothing); it writes a fixed set of rendered root files (`package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `main.ts`, `env.d.ts`, `index.html`) plus a preset.
- TCE `.githooks/pre-push` — **v2** (branch policy + context budget + worklog sync), no full-suite gate.
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — refreshes `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` for the current repo (resolves `measure_context.py` local-then-global).
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — existing scaffold suite (temp fixtures, no network); no hook-wiring assertions.
- `../tce-main-street` (evidence repo) — `.githooks/` committed (v2), `core.hooksPath` unset, no thresholds file, no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; `.git/hooks/pre-push` is an unversioned manual copy.
- `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (SorraAgents, `intake_complete`) — owns the unified v3 hook (local→global runner), one-variant `install_pi.sh`, installed-hook upgrade, and the framework `docs/dev/context-budget.md` table.

## Desired change

1. In `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, set `core.hooksPath=.githooks` in generated repos and install the full-suite pre-push hook (the unified v3 content from `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`) instead of the gate-less v2.
2. Generate and commit `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` for generated repos from their measured surface (reuse `measure_context.py --generate-thresholds` via `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh`).
3. Extend `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` with temp-repo assertions (hooks path, hooks-dir resolution, hook content/gate, thresholds validity) and a linked-worktree push test with a stub runner.
4. Roll out to `../tce-main-street`: set `core.hooksPath`, install the full-suite hook, generate thresholds, and verify a `dev` push is gated and produces a full-suite cache entry.
5. Update scaffold docs / `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `README.md` / TCE `docs/dev/context-budget.md`; remove stale claims that game repos cannot have the gate.
6. Document that a fresh clone still needs one activation step (`install_pi.sh` or `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — set `core.hooksPath`, install the unified hook, seed thresholds.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — TCE hook template to align with the unified v3 full-suite variant (coordinate content with `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`; single source of truth, no divergent copy).
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — threshold-generation entry point.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — hook wiring + thresholds + linked-worktree tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (TCE-owned notes), `README.md` — scaffold/hook docs.
- **Not this item (SorraAgents, owned by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`):** `scripts/install_pi.sh`, `.githooks/pre-push.v2`, framework `docs/dev/context-budget.md`.

## Related work

- **`SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` — blocking.** "Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner" (SorraAgents, `intake_complete`): delivers the unified v3 hook (local→global runner), one-variant `install_pi.sh`, installed-hook upgrade, and the framework docs table. This item consumes that design.
- **`MS-0MVTI7F5R009OQ14`** — `tce-main-street` git hooks inactivity (open): game-side repair of that checkout; the producer deferred the full-suite gate and scaffold wiring to this engine item (answers Q1=c, Q3=a).
- **`SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM`** — original reason non-SorraAgents projects get the v2 hook (they lack `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); superseded by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` resolving the global runner.
- **`SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35`** — AI_Hell v2 rollout: precedent for wiring a real project and verifying the gate end-to-end.
- **`SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61` / `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`** — scope-aware test gate and the "full suite first runs at the dev-push gate" deferral this item makes real for game repos.
- **`SA-0MT1WUEIT006U1HC`** — automated hook wiring via `install_pi.sh`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — hook blocks every game push.** A runner-resolution bug would stop all `dev` pushes. Mitigate with stub-runner tests, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, and an explicit fail-closed message naming the remedy. (Unified hook design owned by the SA item.)
- **Risk — hook drift between TCE's template and SorraAgents' hook.** Mitigate by consuming the SA item's content as the single source of truth and documenting the coordination; do not fork the hook.
- **Risk — suite duration at push time.** A game full suite is minutes; acceptable at one `dev` push per work item; the runner cache makes repeat pushes cheap.
- **Risk — host-wide test-slot contention** when a hook holds the runner's lock. Rely on the runner's bounded lock timeout.
- **Assumption — global runner availability.** Game-machine installs include the test skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); the fail-closed message names `install_pi.sh` when it is missing.
- **Assumption — scaffold regeneration is safe.** Setting `core.hooksPath` is local config; a fresh clone still needs one activation step (documented).
- **Scope-creep risk:** porting every game repo now, redesigning the context-budget measurement, or editing SorraAgents is out of scope; one rollout repo proves the path.

## Appendix: Research & clarifying questions

Research performed during intake (2026-11-03):

- **Repository split confirmed.** The files named in this brief are not all in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo:
  - `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` and `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` live in **Tableau-Card-Engine** (the earlier `core/scripts/...` path was the view from a game repo where `core/` is the TCE submodule). Grep confirms the scaffold has **no** `githooks` / `hooksPath` / `thresholds` handling today, and writes a fixed set of rendered root files.
  - `scripts/install_pi.sh`, `.githooks/pre-push` (v3), `.githooks/pre-push.v2`, `tests/test_pre_push_context_budget_gate.py` and the framework `docs/dev/context-budget.md` live in the **SorraAgents** framework repo (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`), **not** TCE.
- **Overlapping open work item found.** `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` — "Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner" (SorraAgents, `open`, `intake_complete`, type `chore`) already covers the original brief's AC2 (local→global runner resolution), AC3 (one hook variant from `install_pi.sh`, drop the v2 fallback) and the framework docs variant-table update. Its approach is a **single unified v3 hook**, so a separate `.githooks/pre-push.game` / "v4 unified hook" is unnecessary.
- **Duplicate check performed** (`wl search` on "git hooks pre-push", "install_pi hook", "scaffold hooksPath", "context budget thresholds"): no *completed* duplicate exists; the only overlap is the open SA item above. Scope reconciled per Q1 below.
- **Evidence repo state re-verified** in `../tce-main-street` (2026-11-03): `.githooks/` committed (v2 hook), `core.hooksPath` unset, `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` absent, no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, and `.git/hooks/pre-push` is an unversioned manual copy.

### Clarifying questions (answered)

- **Q1 — Scope reconciliation with `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`.** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-03): **(a)** narrow this CG item to the game-repo scaffold wiring (AC1) + rollout verification (AC3) + worktree test (AC2), and mark it **blocked-by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Repo ownership / cross-project edits.** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-03): **(a)** this CG item edits the **Tableau-Card-Engine repo only** (scaffold + its tests + TCE docs); the framework hook and `install_pi.sh` edits are owned by `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Hook variant shape.** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-03): **(a)** one **unified v3 hook** that resolves the runner local-then-global (no separate game variant). Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MUFIBB2X008A136** – implement.py finish pushes from the stale main checkout, failing the context-budget gate (completed)
- **CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ** – AGENTS.md exceeds context-budget threshold, blocking all pushes to dev (completed)
- **CG-0MUMAIIT40002MRP** – Update AGENTS.md for the split multi-repo structure and cross-repo change guidance (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: absent, ac4, ac5, acceptable, acceptance (+337 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, active, agent, align (+261 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: ac2, active, agent, align, also (+208 more)

## Goal

As the engine maintainer, I want the cross-repo facts that three `in_review`
items depend on recorded **inside this repository**, so their audits can verify
the evidence read-only (the audit runner deliberately does not read sibling
checkouts or sibling worklog stores, SA-0MUI5ZYO6002W3KD / SA-0MVPDTSRV0049KW2)
and the v0.1.23 release can proceed on evidence rather than a manual override.

Created from the blocked release audit gate (`/skill:ship release`, 2026-11-03).
Blocker for: `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN`, `CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I`,
`CG-0MVZJ35EV00690W5` (each re-audited to a single `partial` AC whose only gap is
"cannot be verified read-only" — the work itself is complete).

## Scope adjustment (2026-11-03, during implementation)

The operator dispatched a concurrent `/skill:implement CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I`
session that landed the WebGL hand-off record in commit `9fd4774d`
(`docs/ui/renderer-aware-clipping.md` "Downstream switch-over (Main Street
hand-off)" + the `docs/DEVELOPER.md` cross-link). **This item therefore does not
duplicate that work**: it covers only the evidence still missing for the other
two blocked items — the scaffold write-gating consumer verification
(`CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN`) and the soft-sync consumer wiring / build evidence
(`CG-0MVZJ35EV00690W5`).

## Verification performed (2026-11-03)

## Key Files
